newsitem.title: USA: Italy intends to be an EMU founder in 1999 -Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Italy intends to be an EMU founder in 1999 -Ciampi.

text.p: Italy reaffirmed Tuesday its intention to be among the founders of a single European currency and said it was undertaking an extraordinary effort to meet conditions for European currency and monetary union.
"We intend to be among the founders of the EMU in 1999," Treasury and Budget Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi told the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.
"Our new budget target is to reach a total deficit to GDP ratio of three percent in 1997," Ciampi said.
The Maastricht criteria for joining the EMU sets a three percent deficit to GDP ceiling.

He said 60 percent of the reduction in Italy's budget deficit would result from measures already detailed in the budget outline passed by Parliament last Friday, while the remaining 40 percent would be itemized by year-end.
He was referring to last Friday's budget that aims to trim 62.5 trillion lire from the deficit.

When the entire budget, including a 12 trillion lire one-time tax, was implemented, "our budget will be and will remain in order. The structural causes of inflation will have been eradicated," Ciampi said.
Financial markets had reacted favourably to the budget and Ciampi said "significantly lower nominal and real rates are now in sight."

Lower interest rates could further help lower budget deficits but none have been factored into the figures, he said. They would constitute additional savings over and above those already foreseen in the budget.
Ciampi also reaffirmed that the Italian government is "going ahead with the programs of privatization and deregulation of the economy."
Along with adhering to the EMU convergence path, Italy was also bent on reducing unemployment, Ciampi said.
He concluded by saying Italy would be ready by 1999 "to be an active part of the European Union" which was designed at Maastricht as "an area of stability and growth..."
